## Proposed change

I propose we fall back on the empty string title `''` in the apprise notifier, rather than the default title of `'Home Assistant'`, in the case that the title is missing. Apprise allows empty titles, so the empty string is a more natural default.

I'm not entirely sure the best place to test this code, but I also am not necessarily sure it needs a test. It just swaps out one value (`ATTR_TITLE_DEFAULT`, i.e. `"Home Assistant"`) for another value of the same type (`""`).

## Proposed change

  Exposes the attribute exposed by ```monarchmoneycommunity==1.5.2``` (just updated for this purpose) ownedByuser. This allows the user in HomeAssistant to see which user owns which account. In Monarch it's common that multiple users have access to one account, especially on family accounts, this allows the user in HomeAssistant to differentiate which account is which.

Multiple users on one monarch account and account owner assignment in Monarch is a feature that they have just released earlier this year.

- New optional `on_health` callback on the resilient subscriptions (and the
  `subscribe_*_resilient` factories), reporting connection-state transitions,
  plus a `healthy` property. This is groundwork for the integration's
  upcoming `entity-unavailable` quality-scale support (not consumed yet).
- Fixed a liveness gap in the subscription supervisor: after a failed
  reconnect, the watch stayed dead if the network recovered between
  supervisor ticks with no token refresh; it is now re-established on the
  next healthy tick.

Links:

- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/aioaquarite/0.9.0/
- Changelog: https://github.com/fdebrus/aioaquarite/blob/main/CHANGES.md
- Full diff: https://github.com/fdebrus/aioaquarite/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0

With this change, the nexia integration creates entities corresponding to the RoomIQ sensors reported by the nexia library:

- temperature
- humidity
- battery level, if sensor has battery

These entities are created in a zone only when more than 1 RoomIQ sensor is present in that zone. When enabled, these entities register with the nexia library to monitor RoomIQ sensor state updates. This causes each Nexia Home update to also fetch the current RoomIQ sensor states for this zone, adding 5–40 seconds of latency and additional network traffic. To avoid silently doing so, these entities are disabled by default.

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

Fix the target temperature reported by ESPHome climate entities in `auto` mode.

Since #151897 the set points are hidden in `auto` mode, which leaves the entity without any usable temperature control:

- **Single set point devices** report `temperature: null` in `auto`, even though they advertise `TARGET_TEMPERATURE` and `async_set_temperature` happily applies a single set point in that mode. The dial becomes read-only in the UI (#178642).
- **Two point capable devices** report `temperature`, `target_temp_low` **and** `target_temp_high` as `null` in `auto`, so the frontend renders no control at all. The ESPHome `thermostat` component actively uses both set points in `auto` when it supports heat/cool ([`thermostat_climate.cpp`](https://github.com/esphome/esphome/blob/dev/esphome/components/thermostat/thermostat_climate.cpp#L135-L137)), and the write path already accepts `target_temp_low`/`target_temp_high` in `auto` - only the read back was missing.

`auto` is no longer special cased. What is reported now depends only on whether the device can use two set points, and on whether the current mode uses a single one:

| feature flags | mode | `temperature` | `target_temp_low` / `high` | UI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none (single set point) | any, incl. `auto` | set point | not exposed | single handle |
| `SUPPORTS_TWO_POINT` | `heat` / `cool` | low / high | exposed | single handle |
| `SUPPORTS_TWO_POINT` | `heat_cool` / `auto` / `off` | `null` | exposed | two handles |
| `REQUIRES_TWO_POINT` | any | not exposed | exposed | two handles |

The single handle behaviour for `heat`/`cool` added in #151897 is unchanged, and devices that require two set points (`bang_bang`) keep the range in every mode, so #153331 does not regress.

`async_set_temperature` needs no change: it already rejects a single set point for two point devices outside `heat`/`cool`, which matches the read model above.

## Proposed change

RA3 and HomeWorks QSX processors expose relay and contact-closure driven covers as zones
with `ControlType: OpenCloseStop`. These zones support only Raise, Lower and Stop, and
report no level.

Without an explicit mapping they fall back to `LutronCasetaShade`, which advertises
`SET_POSITION` and drives open/close through `set_value`. `OpenCloseStop` zones do not
accept a level, so open and close would not reach the hardware. Their `current_state` is
`-1`, so the cover would also report an invalid position and appear permanently closed.

This adds `LutronCasetaOpenCloseStopCover`:

- supports `OPEN | CLOSE | STOP` only, so no position control is offered
- routes open and close through `raise_cover` / `lower_cover` rather than `set_value`
- sets `_attr_is_closed = None`, since these zones report no position
- sets no device class, because the control type describes the command interface
  rather than the physical load

**Dependency:** discovery of these zones requires
[pylutron-caseta#208](https://github.com/gurumitts/pylutron-caseta/pull/208), merged to
`dev` on 2026-08-08 but not yet released. The currently pinned `pylutron-caseta==0.29.0`
does not classify `OpenCloseStop` as a cover, so this change is inert until a release
containing it is pinned. It can therefore merge independently of that release.

**Testing:** verified against a HomeWorks QSX processor with `OpenCloseStop` zones, using a
custom component built from this branch with the library installed from `dev`. Entities are
created with `supported_features == OPEN | CLOSE | STOP`, expose no `current_position`
attribute, report state `unknown`, and `cover.close_cover` / `cover.open_cover` drive the
hardware in both directions.

Avoid fetching the BSB-LAN domestic-hot-water (DHW) schedule during every slow coordinator update.

The schedule changes infrequently, so it is cached and refreshed only during setup and after a schedule write. Transient schedule-fetch errors are retried on a later update, while unsupported schedules stop retrying. Refresh generations ensure an overlapping schedule write cannot discard a newer refresh request.

This reduces unnecessary BSB-LAN/serial-bus traffic while keeping the cached schedule current after changes.

## Proposed change

This adds DHCP discovery to the EARN-E P1 Meter integration.

**DHCP discovery**

- Adds a DHCP hostname matcher (`energiemonitor-*`) so meters are discovered
  automatically and offered to the user as a discovery flow.
- Implements `async_step_dhcp`: it validates the discovered host, sets the
  serial as the unique ID, and stores the MAC address.
- Adds a MAC fast-path: when a discovered MAC matches an existing entry, the
  entry's host/MAC are updated and reloaded without re-validating.
- Stores the MAC in the coordinator and adds it to the device's
  `connections`, so the device links to the network device in Home Assistant.

The sensor-creation fix that was previously bundled here has been split into
#177027 and removed from this PR.

Key features:
- Adds `HotSpringLightEntity` for each enabled light zone on the spa.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug

  additional information section.
-->
Fix an issue where `TrackerEntity.state_attributes` defaulted to exporting `in_zones: []` even when `self.__in_zones` was `None` (i.e. when the device tracker does not report GPS coordinates or zone membership).

Exporting an empty list `[]` when `in_zones` is absent breaks the fallback logic in `person`:
When a device tracker (such as `mqtt` device_tracker without coordinates) reports state `home`, `TrackerEntity.state_attributes` set `in_zones: []` instead of omitting the attribute. When a `person` entity parses this source tracker state in `_parse_source_state`, it checks `if in_zones is None and state.state == STATE_HOME:` to synthesize `in_zones = ["zone.home"]` for non-GPS / state-only trackers. Because `in_zones` was `[]` instead of `None`, this check was bypassed, leaving `person.attributes.in_zones` empty.

With this fix, `TrackerEntity.state_attributes` only includes `in_zones` when `self.__in_zones is not None`.

## Proposed change

The `created` column was filled from `datetime.now()`, which reads the machine's time zone. Home Assistant never changes the process time zone — `set_default_time_zone()` only sets its own default, there is no `TZ`/`tzset()` anywhere — so on a container started without `TZ` this writes UTC into the user's sheet while the installation is configured for somewhere else, and the string carries nothing to say which zone it is.

`dt_util.now()` uses the configured zone instead, and being aware, `str()` renders the offset.

This does change what lands in the sheet, so it is worth being explicit: for an installation configured as `America/Los_Angeles`, `2024-01-15 12:30:45.123456` becomes `2024-01-15 04:30:45.123456-08:00`. The added test sets a different zone and asserts the value follows it.

## Proposed change

When `_setup_vicare_api` returns zero online devices (because every
known device reports `isOnline() == False`), `async_setup_entry` now
raises `ConfigEntryNotReady` instead of completing with an empty
`runtime_data.devices` list. HA core will then retry setup with its
usual exponential backoff.

Symptom this fixes: after a power outage, the Viessmann gateway can
take a few minutes longer to come back online than Home Assistant.
ViCare currently completes setup during that window with no devices
attached. Pre-existing entities (from previous sessions) stay
permanently `unavailable` until the user reloads the integration
manually. With this change the integration self-heals as soon as the
gateway is reachable again.

If some devices are online and others offline, behaviour is unchanged
(online ones are set up, offline ones are skipped as before).

Exposes the SwitchBot roller shade's motor mode through the cover `speed` parameter added in #176231.

The roller shade entity now sets `CoverEntityFeature.SPEED` and declares `supported_speeds` of `performance` and `quiet`, and maps the selected speed onto the PySwitchbot motor mode (BLE mode byte `00` for performance, `01` for quiet) in `open`, `close` and `set_position`. Speed validation is handled by the cover entity, so an unsupported value raises `ServiceValidationError` before anything reaches the device. Omitting the speed keeps the existing behaviour of running in performance mode. No dependency bump is needed — the motor mode parameter has been available since [pySwitchbot 2.2.0](https://github.com/sblibs/pySwitchbot/compare/2.1.0...2.2.0) and dev currently pins 2.4.1.

An earlier version of this PR added a `roller_shade_quiet_mode` config entry option instead, following the `curtain_speed` pattern from #155272. That approach is gone, along with the options flow entry and the 1.2 → 1.3 config entry migration it required, so the diff is now limited to `const.py`, `cover.py`, `strings.json` and `test_cover.py`.

Tests cover:
- Omitting the speed still sends mode `0` to `open`/`close`/`set_position` (tightens the existing assertions in `test_roller_shade_controlling`).
- `performance` → `0` and `quiet` → `1`, parametrized over both speeds (`test_roller_shade_speed`).
- An unsupported speed raises `ServiceValidationError` with the `not_valid_speed` translation key and never reaches the device, parametrized over all three actions (`test_roller_shade_invalid_speed`).

## Add emergency message canceling to Pushover integration

This PR adds the ability to cancel Pushover emergency notifications (priority 2)
from Home Assistant after they have been sent.

It is a revised implementation addressing the architectural concerns raised during
the review of #144891 by @gandy92.

---

The Pushover API returns a unique `receipt` id whenever an emergency message
(priority 2) is sent. This receipt can be used to cancel repeated delivery before
the message is acknowledged or expires.

This PR adds the following on top of the current `dev` branch:

**`const.py`**
- Added `ATTR_TAG`, `ATTR_TAGS`, `SERVICE_CANCEL`

**`notify.py`**
- Added optional `tags` field in `data`: one or more tags can be assigned to an
  outgoing emergency message so it can be identified and cancelled later
- Receipt ids returned by the API are stored per config entry instance, keyed by
  `entry_id`, so that multiple Pushover accounts work independently
- New `_async_cancel_service_handler` iterates over all registered config entry
  instances so that a single `pushover.cancel` call covers all accounts
- New `cancel_by_tag` method handles the blocking API call from the executor

**`__init__.py`**
- Added `async_unload_entry`: removes the config entry's service instance from the
  registry and deregisters `pushover.cancel` when the last entry is unloaded

**`services.yaml`, `strings.json`**
- Added `cancel` action definition with optional `tag` field

### Multi-account support

Each config entry registers its own `PushoverNotificationService` instance under
`hass.data[DOMAIN]["services"][entry_id]`. The `pushover.cancel` service iterates
over all registered instances, so receipts from multiple Pushover accounts are all
reachable through a single service call with the correct tag.

### Multiple emergency messages with the same tag

Each `send_message` call returns a unique receipt id from the Pushover API. All
receipts are stored independently in `_receipt_tags`. Calling `pushover.cancel`
with a tag cancels every stored receipt that carries that tag, so sending two
emergency messages with the same tag and then cancelling will correctly cancel both.

### Why BaseNotificationService instead of NotifyEntity

The reviewer on #144891 suggested migrating to `NotifyEntity` first. However,
`NotifyEntity.async_send_message` only receives `message` and `title` - the
`ATTR_DATA` payload (priority, retry, expire, tags, ttl, attachment, sound, etc.)
is not forwarded by the entity service machinery. A full migration to `NotifyEntity`
would break all existing Pushover-specific parameters and is a separate, larger
refactor. This PR deliberately keeps `BaseNotificationService` to preserve full
backwards compatibility.

---

## Example usage

Send an emergency notification with a tag:

```yaml
action: notify.pushover
data:
  message: "Motion detected in garage"
  data:
    priority: 2
    retry: 30
    expire: 3600
    tags: garage_alarm
```

Cancel it later (e.g. when the alarm is cleared):

```yaml
action: pushover.cancel
data:
  tag: garage_alarm
```

Cancel all tracked emergency notifications at once:

```yaml
action: pushover.cancel
```

Multiple tags can be assigned to a single message:

```yaml
data:
  priority: 2
  retry: 30
  expire: 3600
  tags:
    - garage_alarm
    - building_a
```

## Proposed change

Migrate `zhong_hong` off the YAML climate platform onto a config entry.

The integration was configured as a climate platform in YAML and kept no state of its own: the gateway connection was opened from the platform setup, every entity polled the library object it was given, and a command the gateway refused was dropped on the floor.

Setting it up from a config entry moves the connection into a coordinator, which discovers the air conditioners behind the gateway, starts the library's listener thread, and hands its pushes to the entities. Polling stays as a minute-interval fallback for pushes missed while the connection was down, and a gateway that stops answering now makes the entities unavailable instead of leaving them on their last known state. A command is followed by a re-read a few seconds later, because a unit reports the new state itself but that report can go missing.

Existing YAML configuration is imported and raises the deprecation repair issue. **The import deliberately does not check that the gateway can be reached.** The gateway accepts a single TCP connection at a time and can still be holding the one from the previous run, so a restart is exactly when a reachability check is most likely to fail for reasons that say nothing about the configuration — and because the YAML platform is only set up once per start, that failure would strand the user on YAML until they restarted again. Setting up the entry retries on its own, which is where an unreachable gateway belongs. This is not hypothetical; it is what happens on my own installation.

Entities registered by the YAML platform are migrated onto gateway-scoped unique IDs on setup — the old ones carried only the bus address, so two gateways with a unit at the same address (commonly `(1, 1)`) collided and Home Assistant dropped the second entity. The migration preserves each entity's `entity_id`, so an imported installation keeps its entity IDs, its automations and its recorded history. Only entities this entry owns are moved, so an entry whose gateway is offline cannot claim another's history.

Two smaller fixes ride along, both in code this PR rewrites anyway:

- Two of the five fan speeds the protocol can address had no mapping, because `FAN_MEDIUM` and `FAN_MIDDLE` were both mapped to `MID` and the latter won. They reached the user under the names used on the wire, `MIDLOW` and `MIDHIGH`, which are not valid fan modes. They are now named `medium_low` and `medium_high`.
- Commands the gateway does not acknowledge raise a translated `HomeAssistantError` rather than failing silently.

Tests cover the component fully. Verified against a real gateway with six indoor units, including the YAML import path on an installation that had been running the YAML platform.

# Add button platform to NeoPool

## Proposed change

Adds a `button` platform for the NeoPool pool controller so users can trigger device-maintenance actions from Home Assistant. This is the next platform in the series that incrementally ports the remaining controls from the upstream library, after the sensor (#173779) and light (#176039) platforms.

The platform registers three action buttons:

- **Synchronize device time** writes the current Home Assistant wall-clock to the controller's clock, via the library's `async_sync_device_time`. A small helpers module is introduced with `prepare_device_time`, which encodes the current local time into the device's timestamp format; it is consumed by this button.
- **Clear error messages** clears the controller's active error and alarm messages via `async_clear_errors`.
- **Reset cell runtime counter** resets the partial cell-runtime counter used to track electrolytic cell wear, via `async_reset_user_counters`. It is gated on the hydrolysis module, categorised as configuration, and disabled by default because it clears a wear counter the user may want to keep.

Presses call the library client directly and then request a coordinator refresh so the UI reflects any resulting state. Communication errors (`NeoPoolError`, `OSError`, `TimeoutError`) are surfaced as a translated `HomeAssistantError`, reusing the existing `modbus_communication_error` message.

## Proposed change

Convert 15 single-channel sensor subclasses in the `homematicip_cloud` integration to a description-driven generic entity, following the pattern established for binary sensors in #171825. Each sensor type is now declared once as a module-level `HmipSensorDescription` and dispatched per device type via a new `SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS_BY_DEVICE` mapping. Net change: `-26` lines despite covering 15 classes, with stronger typing (typed-generic descriptions) and dropping most of the per-class `getattr` boilerplate.

The description schema adds two callable fields beyond the binary sensor pattern:
- `extra_attrs_fn`: for sensors that expose extra state attributes (temperature offset, wind direction, illumination peaks, left/right counter).
- `icon_fn`: for sensors that need a dynamic icon (heating thermostat valve state). The parent class still wins the icon contest first so `lowBat` and similar device-level flags keep their icons.

**Migrated:** `TemperatureSensor`, `HumiditySensor`, `AbsoluteHumiditySensor`, `IlluminanceSensor`, `PowerSensor`, `EnergySensor`, `WindspeedSensor`, `TodayRainSensor`, `TemperatureExternalSensorCh1/Ch2/Delta`, `AccesspointDutyCycle`, `HeatingThermostat`, `PassageDetectorDeltaCounter`, `TiltAngleSensor`.

**Deferred to a follow-up PR** (multi-channel or special-setup, intentionally out of scope here): `SoilMoistureSensor`, `SoilTemperatureSensor`, `WaterFlowSensor`, `WaterVolumeSensor`, `WaterVolumeSinceOpenSensor`, `FloorTerminalBlockMechanicChannelValve`, the ESI family. `TiltStateSensor` and `HmipSmokeDetectorSensor` are already description-driven and untouched.

Entity `unique_id`s, `entity_id`s and friendly names are preserved exactly: each description's `key` matches the previous `feature_id`, and `translation_key`s carry forward the existing display names where the post-derived name differs from the HA `device_class` default (Windspeed, Absolute Humidity, Today Rain, Duty Cycle, Heating, Tilt Angle, Channel N Temperature, Delta Temperature).

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/166672 for background.

I believe what is happening here is that, during startup:
- The tracked sensor changes state before history stats sensor sets up its state listener, which happens at homeassistant start.
- History stats queries the recorder at startup to get the history of state changes, but this is either done before the tracked sensor changes state, or after it changes state, but before the pending state changes are flushed, so the recorder query doesn't see it.
- Since history stats doesn't get notified of the state change (happened before listener setup), and the state change isn't reflected in its recorder query, it just continues happily forever assuming the sensor is in its pre-restart state, instead of the new state that changed during start.


I think to fix this what we can do is that once we setup the state change listener, we can just query the source sensor state one time from the hass state machine, and that will close any holes where the state changed during startup. 

I observed that this fixes the issue in my development testing. I did not write a test because it would be very contrived and just catering to my assumption of how the startup sequence looks, but I'd like to get a confirmation that this sounds like the right way to fix this before we codify a test that explicitly follows this assumption.

An LG SG10TY advertises 13 equalisers, `ai_eq_list: [19, 0, 7, 26, 21, 6, 22, 14, 5, 15, 23, 24, 25]`, but the entity only offered 9 of them. `temescal.equalisers` holds 23 names (0-22), and both the list and the current value guarded against anything above that by dropping it:

```python
return sorted(
    temescal.equalisers[equaliser]
    for equaliser in self._equalisers
    if equaliser < len(temescal.equalisers)
)
```

Nothing is logged, so the soundbar simply looks like it has four fewer sound modes. Worse, selecting one of those on the physical remote made `sound_mode` return `None`, so the entity reported no sound mode at all rather than an unrecognised one.

The name tables live in `temescal`, which has been archived and read-only since 2023-03-23, so they will not grow to cover newer models. The integration has to be able to cope with indices it cannot name.

Unmapped indices are now given a name and resolved back through the list the device offered, so they show up in the list and can be selected. `source` and `source_list` are built the same way against `temescal.functions` (21 entries), so they go through the same helper rather than being left inconsistent.

`Unknown (23)` is the placeholder suggested in the issue. It is deliberately model agnostic: new models will keep reporting new indices, so this stops them disappearing regardless. Should the real names for these become known, they can be layered on top without changing this structure.

One existing behaviour is kept on purpose: `select_source` used to accept any name in the library table even when the device never offered it, so the lookup still falls back to the table. There is a test for it.

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

`source_list` returned the device names in whatever order Spotify sent them, and that order is not stable between calls. The list ends up in `capability_attributes`, which the entity registry stores, so every reshuffle of an unchanged set of devices is written as a capability change and fires `entity_registry_updated` with `changes: {"capabilities": ...}`.

The device coordinator polls every five minutes, so this repeats indefinitely for a device list that never changed. On the reporting instance that was roughly 288 registry updates a day, each one waking anything that keeps a cache of the 3,215 entities in that house.

Sorting the names keeps an unchanged set of devices identical between polls.

The sort is in the property rather than in the coordinator on purpose: `async_media_play` falls back to `self.devices.data[0]` when nothing is playing, and reordering the coordinator data would quietly change which device that picks.

Two things this does not change. Duplicate device names still produce duplicate entries, exactly as before. The issue also mentions Samsung TV entities churning on `supported_features`, but that is a different integration and an `IntFlag` whose order cannot vary, so it is not the same bug.

Setting up an MCP server against an SSE endpoint logs a blocking call warning:

```
Detected blocking call to load_verify_locations ... inside the event loop by integration 'mcp'
at homeassistant/components/mcp/coordinator.py, line 84: sse_client(url=url, headers=headers)
```

`mcp_client` tries the streamable HTTP transport first and falls back to SSE when the server answers 405. The streamable transport is handed a Home Assistant httpx client via `create_async_httpx_client`, but the SSE fallback was called with only a URL and headers, so the SDK used its own `create_mcp_http_client()`. That builds a fresh `httpx.AsyncClient`, which reads the CA bundle from disk while on the event loop.

`sse_client` accepts an `httpx_client_factory`, so the fix is to supply one. It cannot simply reuse `create_async_httpx_client` though: `sse_client` takes the client as `async with`, so the SDK closes it, and the `aclose` of a Home Assistant managed client is wrapped by `warn_use`. Passing one would swap the blocking call for a usage report and connections that are never closed. The factory therefore builds a plain client that the SDK owns, on top of the shared SSL context that is pre-warmed at import.

The ALPN protocols are passed explicitly for the same reason `create_async_httpx_client` does it: httpx mutates the context with `set_alpn_protocols()`, so the contexts are bucketed per protocol set. The client does not enable http2, so it takes the `SSL_ALPN_HTTP11` bucket.

Checked that the resulting client keeps the SDK's behaviour otherwise: `follow_redirects` is enabled, and the headers and timeout passed by `sse_client` come through (`connect=5`, `read=300`).

The test asserts what the report describes, that driving the SSE path and then building a client never calls `SSLContext.load_verify_locations`. It fails without the change, since no factory is passed at all.

<!--

Renames the setpoint added in #180241 and its switch from #180261. "AC Power limit" doesn't affect battery charging power - the name shall reflect that.

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `Power limit` | `AC power limit` |
| `Power limiting` | `AC power limiting` |

`WMaxLimPct` caps what the inverter puts out **on AC**, whatever that then serves. It is *not* a feed-in limit: at a 6 kW cap with 4 kW of household load, 2 kW is exported; with 7 kW of load nothing is exported and the cap still applies. Fronius describes it as limiting "the device's maximum possible output power". A real export limit is *Dynamic power reduction*, which measures at the grid connection point and is a separate control source with its own priority — not this register.

`Power limit` said neither which side it acts on nor that self-consumption counts against it. This integration already names values by side — `AC power`, `AC current`, `DC voltage`, `MPPT 1 DC power` — so the prefix form follows the existing convention, and `AC power limit` reads as the cap on the `AC power` sensor that is already there.

Rename only: no logic changes, 18 lines across seven files.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

WLED can limit current globally, or per LED output. With per output limiters the global power budget is unset, so the device reports `maxpwr: 0` while it keeps estimating and reporting the current it draws:

```json
"leds": { "count": 330, "pwr": 3193, "maxpwr": 0, ... }
```

The estimated current sensor was gated on that power budget rather than on the estimate it actually reads, so the entity was never created for these devices. Downstream consumers that rely on it (the reporter uses Powercalc) break as a result.

It is gated on the estimate itself now. Two details from the firmware back that up:

- `maxpwr` is reported as `currentMilliamps() > 0 ? ablMilliampsMax() : 0` ([json.cpp](https://github.com/wled/WLED/blob/main/wled00/json.cpp#L726)), so it can only be non-zero when `pwr` is. Checking both fields would be equivalent to checking `pwr` alone.
- The estimate adds a standby current of 1 mA per LED ([bus_manager.cpp](https://github.com/wled/WLED/blob/main/wled00/bus_manager.cpp#L205)), so it does not drop to zero while the strip is off. The entity will not come and go depending on when the integration is set up.

The max current sensor keeps its existing check, since that one does report the power budget.

`test_no_current_measurement` covered a device that reports no power budget but still reports an estimate, which is the case being fixed here. It now clears both, which is what a device with automatic brightness limiting fully disabled sends.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Clearing every trusted proxy in the network settings and saving fails with `some but not all values in the same group of inclusion 'proxy'`. Turning the reverse proxy off through the UI is impossible; the only way out is to keep a dummy CIDR in the list.

`HTTP_STORAGE_SCHEMA` inherited `vol.Inclusive` from the YAML schema, so `use_x_forwarded_for` and `trusted_proxies` have to be present together or not at all. The network settings form drops empty multi-value fields before sending, so `use_x_forwarded_for: false` arrives on its own and the schema refuses it.

Both keys are plain `vol.Optional` now. Absent stays absent, so `_DEFAULT_CONFIG`, the store migration and the YAML path are unaffected.

The save path gains the check that actually matters instead: enabling `use_x_forwarded_for` with an empty proxy list is rejected. That combination is accepted today and is a quiet footgun, since the forwarded middleware then refuses every proxied request as coming from an untrusted proxy. The check lives on the websocket command rather than in the storage schema, so a config stored by an older version can never fail validation during migration and get discarded.

The YAML schema in `__init__.py` keeps its `vol.Inclusive`; that contract is documented and unrelated to the reported problem.

Bumps `fumis` from 0.4.0 to 0.4.1.

Some stove controllers report `command` as `null` instead of an integer. The model declared it as a plain `int`, so deserialization blew up with a mashumaro `InvalidFieldValue` and the config flow bailed out with an unknown error. The field is now `int | None`, defaulting to `None`.

The `command` field is transient (it resets once the controller acknowledges it) and is not used anywhere in the integration, so no changes are needed on the Home Assistant side.

`fetch_all_features()` requires an accessor in PyViCare 2.61.0, so every coordinator refresh raised `TypeError` and setup failed. Pass the device's accessor.

The test mock accepted any signature, which is why this was not caught; it now mirrors the real one.

Nothing released is affected, the bug only exists on `dev` since today, but if it ships as is ViCare will not set up at all in 2026.9. If the 2026.9 beta is already cut, this needs to go into it.

@joostlek this is a bug in #173776, which you merged earlier today. It slipped past me because my local instance runs the follow-up branch (#176163) on top, and that one already passes the accessor. Sorry for the extra round.

## Proposed change

`pylitterbot`'s WebSocket monitor logs an error and a full traceback on every Home Assistant restart:

```
ERROR (MainThread) [pylitterbot.transport] Unexpected error in WebSocket monitor; reconnecting in 1.0s
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../pylitterbot/transport.py", line 155, in _run
    await self._connect()
  File ".../pylitterbot/transport.py", line 189, in _connect
    async with session.ws_connect(**config) as ws:
  File ".../aiohttp/client.py", line 581, in _request
    raise RuntimeError("Session is closed")
RuntimeError: Session is closed
```

Config entries are not unloaded when Home Assistant stops. `ConfigEntries._async_shutdown` calls `entry.async_shutdown()`, which only cancels the retry-setup timer, so the `await account.disconnect()` in `async_unload_entry` never runs at shutdown. The account's monitor task is created inside the library with a bare `asyncio.create_task`, so it is not one of the background tasks Home Assistant cancels either. It is still running at `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_CLOSE`, when the shared aiohttp session is detached underneath it.

`EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP` fires two stages earlier, while the session is still usable, so listening for it disconnects the account cleanly and the error no longer occurs.

This matches the pattern already used by `zwave_js`, `unifiprotect`, `smartthings` and `homekit_controller`.

Adds two `button` entities, both wired to methods the sofar-modbus
library already exposes on `SofarInverter`:
- **RTC sync** — writes the current time to the inverter's clock
  (`async_set_time()`). Applies to both PV and hybrid. The
  confirmation sensor for this (`sync_rtc_result`) only exists on
  hybrids, so a PV inverter gets a working button with no read-back —
  matching the vendor's own upstream behavior for this control.
- **IV curve scan** — triggers a sweep of the PV strings' I-V curves
  (`async_start_iv_curve_scan()`), hybrid only. No result register to
  read back, so it doesn't request a coordinator refresh afterward.
Both are `EntityCategory.CONFIG`: infrequent maintenance/calibration
actions, not day-to-day controls.

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Bumps sofar-modbus from 0.5.0 to 0.6.0.

0.6.0 stops re-reading the identity block (serial number, firmware versions) on every settings poll and instead reads it once during setup, since none of that data changes. Full changelog: https://github.com/darkrain-nl/sofar-modbus/releases/tag/0.6.0

Because we always pass a known serial_number into SofarInverter(...), the library's own automatic identity read never triggers for us, so this PR also adds one explicit await device.identity.async_update() call during setup and drops the now-dead coordinator logic that used to catch identity off a settings refresh (it can no longer appear there). Without this companion change, hw_version/sw_version would silently stop being populated for every existing installation.

One resilience note: if that one-time identity read fails at setup, it is no longer retried automatically on the next settings poll (the library never touches identity again). Recovery now requires a reload, matching how 0.6.0 treats identity. hw_version/sw_version are metadata only, so this does not affect any other sensor or entity.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug

The Teslemetry energy live status, site info and V2 tariff coordinators each poll the Tesla Fleet REST API on a 30-second timer, even though the Teslemetry server already polls and caches this data and can push it over the existing account SSE stream.

This moves those three coordinators onto the stream:

- The account stream is now created whenever there is at least one eligible vehicle **or** energy site, so energy-only accounts open it too (and gain the credit sensors that come with it). The constructor is given an explicit topic allowlist of exactly the events the integration consumes.
- Each energy site registers `live_status`, `site_info` and `tariff_content_v2` listeners before the stream starts.
- Slim `site_info` and the V2 tariff are treated as two independently replaceable partitions and recomposed into the existing flattened coordinator view, so a removed field or a cleared tariff no longer lingers.
- Initial REST reads are kept for deterministic setup/auth handling and manual recovery; the recurring 30-second live/info polls are removed.

No entity IDs, unique IDs, state classes, units or enabled-by-default choices change, so automations and long-term statistics see identical values. No dependency bump is required — `teslemetry-stream` 0.10.0 (already pinned) provides the energy-site listeners.

## Proposed change

This PR addresses [home-assistant/feature-requests#619](https://github.com/orgs/home-assistant/discussions/619) by giving consumers a way to read the Forecast.Solar production curve outside the Energy dashboard. Today the only path to the time series is the diagnostic dump, which isn't usable from automations, templates, or dashboard cards.

A single new surface is added:

**`forecast_solar.get_forecast` service action** (response-only): returns the cached forecast as two flat maps:

```yaml
watts:
  "2026-06-20T10:00:00+10:00": 4321
  "2026-06-20T10:15:00+10:00": 4587
  ...
wh_period:
  "2026-06-20T10:00:00+10:00": 1080
  "2026-06-20T10:15:00+10:00": 1146
  ...
```

`watts` is the estimated instantaneous power in W keyed by interval start; `wh_period` is the energy produced during the interval that starts at that key. Optional `start` (inclusive), `end` (exclusive), and `resolution` (`"raw"` or `"hourly"`) parameters narrow or aggregate the response. ISO keys carry the site/API timezone offset so consumers parsing the response directly see local-zoned timestamps. Naive `start`/`end` values from the UI datetime selector are interpreted in the forecast zone.

The underlying data is already cached by the coordinator (`Estimate.watts`, `Estimate.wh_period`); only the public surface changes. No upstream library or API changes are required.

### Design

The service-with-response action is the modern HA pattern for exposing time series. It covers all the requested use cases (dashboard cards via a template sensor, automation logic, optimisers, multi-day comparisons) without persisting bulk forecast data in entity state.

### History

An earlier revision of this PR also exposed `watts`/`wh_period` as `_unrecorded_attributes` on `sensor.energy_production_today`. That was dropped in response to review feedback from @karwosts and @klaasnicolaas: even with the recorder excluded, the attribute path ships a large payload to every connected frontend on initial state load and pushes it on every coordinator update. The service action is the preferred surface.

Add a condition option for template entities.  The condition is only available for trigger based template entities and the request comes from [this feature request](https://github.com/orgs/home-assistant/discussions/21).  Users would like the ability to run actions like "get_forecasts" and programatically update the template sensor based on the response.  E.g. if the response is empty, do not update the template entity.

The condition option will block all updates to the entity it's attached to.  This differs from the main section's condition.  The main sections condtion blocks actions and templates from updating.  This condition section only blocks updates to a specific entity after the action section has executed.

```yaml
template:
  - triggers:
      - trigger: time_pattern
        hours: /1
    actions:
      - action: weather.get_forecasts
        data:
          type: hourly
        target:
          entity_id: weather.home
        response_variable: hourly

    sensor:
      - conditions:
        - condition: template
          value_template: "{{ hourly['weather.home'].forecast | length > 0 }}"
        name: Temperature forecast next hour
        unique_id: temperature_forecast_next_hour
        state: >
          {{
            hourly['weather.home'].forecast[0].temperature
          }}
        unit_of_measurement: "°C"    
```

Also users can conditionally split positive and negative values, which is a common request for some energy sensors.  Users no longer need to rely on `this.state` to build the condition within the state template.

```yaml
template:
  - triggers:
      trigger: state
      entity_id: sensor.source_value
    sensor:
      - name: Positive values
        conditions:
          condition: numeric_state
          entity_id: sensor.source_value
          above: 0
        state: "{{ states('sensor.source_value') }}"

      - name: Negative values
```

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

On first boot, the HTTP server serves the onboarding API from bootstrap stage 0, while the hassio integration only loads in stage 1. When the onboarding frontend loads during that window, `/api/onboarding/installation_type` misdetects Supervisor based installations as "Home Assistant Container" (`is_hassio()` is still false).

This is not cosmetic: the frontend fetches the installation type once when onboarding loads and caches it for the whole onboarding session. Restoring a backup during onboarding is then routed through Core's local backup agent (`backup.local`) instead of Supervisor's (`hassio.local`), add-on restore is disabled in the backup data picker, and a wrong "add-ons unsupported" alert is shown — resulting in a silent partial restore on Home Assistant OS.

This PR makes the installation type view wait for the hassio integration using `async_wait_component` — the same pattern `WaitIntegrationOnboardingView` in this file already uses. The wait returns immediately when hassio is not pending setup (e.g. container installations), so no environment check is needed. The wait is safe: hassio's setup-done future is created before stage 0 and resolves even if the config entry lands in `SETUP_RETRY`. This also holds in recovery mode: `SUPERVISOR` in the environment adds hassio to the domains to set up regardless of recovery mode, so the wait behaves like a normal boot there and resolves when hassio setup completes. The frontend does not block on this request, so onboarding UX is unaffected — the response simply arrives a few seconds later with the correct value.

This complements #178677, which ensures Supervisor data is populated within hassio's setup on first boot; without it, waiting for the component alone would not be sufficient.

## Proposed change

This PR fixes an issue where a ZHA device with no entities would not set `via_device_id`.

This is fixed by moving the `via_device_link` out of the base ZHA entity class and into the ZHA gateway proxy's `_async_get_or_create_device_proxy` method, where `sw_version` is also already added, for example.

Note this is **not** related to the recent device entry split. I did notice this weird behavior reviewing  https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/178168 though.

### Tests

A regression test is also added. Note that the diff looks a bit weird but only the one line mentioned below is added to the existing test.

This also adds a one line assert to the `test_device_registry_via_device` test for the change made in:
- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/154004

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

An invalid or revoked access token previously left the config entry permanently retrying setup — silently unavailable, with no recovery path except removing and re-adding the device. With vizaio's typed exception hierarchy the coordinator can now distinguish auth failures from connectivity failures, and the config flow gains both reauth and reconfigure support built on a single shared validation pipeline:

- `VizioAuthError` from any coordinator device call (including the optional/degradable fetches) raises `ConfigEntryAuthFailed`, triggering Home Assistant's standard reauth repair flow.
- The user, reauth, and new reconfigure sources all follow the same code path (`_async_validate_and_continue`): detect the device class, verify the device identity via its serial number, then save directly (speaker, or TV with a working token) or run the existing `pair_tv` PIN step. The sources differ only in which form is shown, whether the device must be new (`user`) or match the existing entry (`reauth`/`reconfigure`), and whether finishing creates or updates the entry (`async_update_reload_and_abort` — no entry recreation, entities and history preserved).
- Reauth validates the stored token first and recovers without pairing when it works again (transient auth failure), otherwise it re-runs PIN pairing and updates the token in place.
- Reconfigure lets the user change the host: the flow verifies the serial number matches the existing entry (aborting with `unique_id_mismatch` otherwise), re-detects the device class, and automatically re-pairs if the stored token is rejected.
- This branch includes the auto device class detection commit from #177642 (its merge-parent); the diff shrinks to just the reauth/reconfigure work once that PR merges.

This satisfies the `reauthentication-flow` (Silver) and `reconfiguration-flow` (Gold) rules of the Integration Quality Scale. It supersedes the standalone reconfigure approach from #177590 per the review discussion there.

## Proposed change

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Follows #180241, which added the Modbus setpoints as `number` entities, with the switches that turn them on and off:

| entity | register |
|---|---|
| Power limiting | `WMaxLim_Ena` (model 123) |
| Battery charge power limiting | `StorCtl_Mod` bit 0 (model 124) |
| Battery discharge power limiting | `StorCtl_Mod` bit 1 |
| Battery grid charging | `ChaGriSet` |

### Off and 100 % are different things

This is the reason the switches are needed at all. Turning a limit **off** does not lift it — the inverter hands control back to the next priority source, which may impose a limit of its own. The Fronius Modbus documentation is explicit:

> Betriebsart wird […] beendet und **auf die nächste Priorität zurückgestellt** (z.B.: Dynamische Leistungsreduzierung)

So holding a limit **on at 100 %** is how a lower-priority source gets overridden, and releasing control is a separate action. Both have to be reachable, and a `number` alone cannot express both.

### A setpoint no longer activates a released limit

In #180241 each setpoint wrote its enable register, because without a switch it would otherwise have done nothing. That is now wrong: someone who deliberately released a limit — to let dynamic power reduction take over — would silently take control back by nudging a number.

A setpoint now writes the enable register **only when the limit is already on**, which the device requires for a change to an active mode to be picked up:

> Um bei einer aktiven Betriebsart Werte zu verändern […] neuen Wert in das entsprechende Register schreiben → die Betriebsart über Register `WMaxLim_Ena` erneut starten

Writing a setpoint while the limit is off still stores it on the device; the switch then applies the stored value, which is the order the documentation prescribes.

### Tests

Both behaviours are covered and were checked to fail without the code that implements them: that a setpoint leaves a released limit released, that it re-enables an active one, and that the two `StorCtl_Mod` switches don't clobber each other's bit.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The registry websocket APIs persist whatever label ids the client sends, with no check against the label registry. Label *cleanup* only runs on label deletion (the `EVENT_LABEL_REGISTRY_UPDATED` listeners), so an id that never existed in the registry — e.g. the frontend's `___no_items_available___` picker sentinel — gets stored permanently and is never cleaned up. Several users hit this on 2026.6 and ended up with helpers that show error icons and a Helpers page that fails to load.

This strips label ids that aren't in the label registry before saving, in the `config/entity_registry/update`, `config/device_registry/update`, and `config/area_registry/create|update` handlers. Because the frontend always sends the full label set, this also self-heals entries that already carry a stale label: the bad id is dropped the next time the entry is saved, with no error surfaced to the user.

## Proposed change

Adds the initial cloud-polling integration for NexBlue EV chargers.

The integration uses the published [nexblue-api](https://github.com/NexBlue-AB/nexblue-api) Python library and provides a configuration flow for NexBlue end-user credentials. It discovers chargers available to the account and exposes read-only charger telemetry, including charging state, power, session and lifetime energy, electrical measurements, and selected diagnostic values.

This initial PR intentionally provides read-only `sensor` and `binary_sensor` platforms. Charging controls and a dedicated reauthentication flow will be proposed separately to keep the initial integration review focused.

The integration refreshes its access token automatically. If the refresh token is invalid, it makes one saved-password login attempt. Authentication failure stops setup rather than repeatedly sending invalid credentials.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug

  additional information section.

Adds all remaining sensors exposed by guntamatic 1.11.0 and organizes them per heating circuit:

- **Per-circuit sub-devices** (HC0–HC8): room temperature, flow temperature, circulation pump and program are grouped on a "Heating circuit N" device linked to the main unit, so circuits can be assigned to different areas. Only circuits that report data create a device.
- **Enum sensors**: heating circulation programs (`off/timer/heat/hibernate/hibernate_to`) and pump operating modes (`auto/off/nonstop`) are exposed as enum sensors with state translations. guntamatic 1.11.0 translates the heater's localized strings to these canonical values in all 10 UI languages.
- Auxiliary pumps were previously configured as percentage measurements while the heater reports string states; they are now enums.
- Buffer stage temperatures, auxiliary pumps, suction fan, air dampers, CO₂ content, interruptions and operating/service time (diagnostic, disabled by default where appropriate).
- `operating_time` is a `DURATION` sensor in hours; `service_date` is a `DATE` sensor (diagnostic, `DATE` device class) reporting the ISO date of the next service, computed as `now()` + days-until-service from the heater (e.g., `2035-07-06` in snapshot).

Notes for review:
- Supersedes #171627 (same feature, rebased onto current dev with dependency changes removed — the bumps landed separately).
- The `status` sensor stays a diagnostic text sensor for now: no complete list of its localized states is available yet; it will become an enum once captured.
- `interruption_1/2` return an empty string when no fault is active; they are diagnostic and disabled by default.
- Each motherboard supports up to 9 circuit slots (`_0`–`_8`); the library only returns values for connected circuits, and entities/devices are only created for those.

## Proposed change
<!--

This PR fixes an issue where transient network failures (such as DNS timeouts) during Google Drive token refreshes resulted in an unhandled exception and a massive traceback in the logs.

**The Problem:**
In `api.py`, `async_get_access_token` was catching *all* `aiohttp.ClientError` exceptions and blindly re-raising them as a generic `HomeAssistantError("authentication_failed")`. 
Because `HomeAssistantError` is not caught by the integration's `DataUpdateCoordinator` wrapper, the error leaked out to the coordinator's catch-all `Exception` block, resulting in an `Unexpected error fetching google_drive data` log and preventing the integration from recovering cleanly.

**The Solution:**
Refined the exception handling in `api.py` to differentiate between true authentication failures and transient network errors:
*   **HTTP 400 Errors:** Triggers `async_start_reauth` and raises `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` (which the coordinator natively understands).
*   **Transient Errors (Setup):** Raises `ConfigEntryNotReady`.
*   **Transient Errors (Runtime):** Performs a bare `raise` of the `ClientError`. The underlying `google_drive_api` library natively catches this and wraps it into an `AuthException` (which inherits from `GoogleDriveApiError`). The coordinator already catches `GoogleDriveApiError` and correctly translates it into a standard, clean `UpdateFailed`.

Added explicit test coverage to `test_init.py` to validate token refresh behavior during normal runtime polling.

If the server goes offline the integration is marked as failed to setup and that entities are no longer provided. It is not uncommon to turn off a server when not in used. These changes removes a sleep during command call and rely on the coordinator instead to check for changes and make the entities unavailable instead. Earlier approach tries to reconnect every 30 second which create a lot of uneccessery error codes in the logs. It also prevent the integration from allowing multiple servers so this could be an initial step for multi server support. The PR include a raise on the polling from 10s to 30seconds (but most likely possible to raise higher)  and a retry timer on 10 minutes.

Also added a helper text to the setup to clarify that http:// is required in the host url.
